messages:
Anya: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a layered rollback protocol for on-prem / air-gapped upgrades. TL;DR: two-phase activation (staged-activate + commit-swap) + compact tombstone manifest + local operator revert. Looking for concerns about DB migrations, cross-mount atomicity, and audit trail.

Devon: Can you sketch the phases? a short sequence/example would help.

Anya: sure, high-level sequence:
1) download & verify bundle -> write a staged-manifest (read-only)
2) extract artifacts into staging/ (never touch live symlinks)
3) staged-activate writes activation.marker -> points to staging-id
4) smoke-run healthchecks against staging endpoints (configurable window)
5) commit-swap atomically flips live symlinks, GC-marks old staging as tombstone
6) tombstone manifest + signature is recorded in local seed cache + ledger for audit/rollback

Maggie: two quick things:
- how atomic is commit-swap on Linux? relying on rename(2) semantics across mounts is risky. :thinking:
- where do tombstones live so offline clusters don't lose them?

Anya: good calls. Implementation notes:
- commit-swap: prefer dual-symlink + single-rename inside same fs for POSIX atomicity.
- cross-mount components: fall back to a swap-transaction file recorded under /var/lib/redwood/transactions/ with an FS-atomic write then fsync; operator CLI does final reconciliation if rename non-atomic.
- tombstones: content-addressed files under /var/lib/redwood/seed/tombstones/<bundle-id>.json plus an append-only operator ledger at /etc/redwood/ledger. The airgap support bundle includes the ledger snapshot for post-mortem.

Sanjay: DB migrations are my big worry. If staging has an irreversible schema change, revert is impossible. How are we gating migrations?

Anya: require migrations to be two-phase by default: compatibility flag + backfill step. For irreversible cases, manifest must include an explicit "irreversible":true marker, which forces an operator consent flow and extends the revert window. We'll also write an irreversible-marker entry into the ledger (signed). Console surfaces a big warning.

Devon: How does verifier/escrow interact? If operator tampers with ledger/tombstone files offline, can we detect later?

Anya: yes — both tombstones and ledger entries are signed. Design: append-only ledger entries include rolling hash chaining and each tombstone manifest contains previous-entry-hash and a signature. Agents verify signatures before trusting tombstones. For Private installs use customer KMS; for Hosted/Dedicated OEM key is used.

Maggie: operator UX: we want a single CLI to "revert to previous" that works offline. No network fetch.

Anya: revert path is local-only by default. Flow: find latest non-tombstoned staging, verify signature, run staged-activate -> commit-swap in reverse. If staging missing, `--force-from-remote` will attempt fetch. Sample CLI: `redwood agent revert --to-previous --dry-run`

Sanjay: multi-component bundles (runtime + modelstore + observer) must be consistent on rollback. Partial rollbacks are a large risk.

Anya: attach bundle-atomic-id and per-component version list to staged-manifest. Coordinator flips components in deterministic order and records per-component result to a local transaction file. On partial failure we auto-tombstone the new partial bundle and surface a single revert action.

Devon: smoke-run window should be short by default but configurable per-manifest route. Default 30s, ops can set 10m for high-risk changes.

Anya: agreed. policy param in manifest: "smoke_run_secs": 30 and Console exposes it. Longer windows push GC and extend revertability.

Maggie: RFC doc edits to add:
- sample ledger format (compact)
- rename-fallback flow for cross-mount swaps
- migration gating + Console/operator prompts
- CLI revert UX examples

Anya: sample ledger line (human-friendly append format):
```
<ts> <bundle-id> <prev-hash> <flags> <sig>
# example
1709001234 bundle::sha256:abc123 prev::sha256:def456 flags::irreversible sig::base64(...)
```

Anya: sample tombstone manifest minimal fields: `bundle_id`, `activated_at`, `prev_entry_hash`, `tombstone_reason`, `signature`

Devon: ops-bot can you open a follow-up ticket with checklist? :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Ticket created: ARCH-1198 "Layered rollback protocol: RFC follow-up + checklist" — assignee: Anya.

Sanjay: also add DR section: if ledger/tombstones corrupted, fallback to seed snapshot + manual restore steps; include sample `rsync` restore playbook.

Anya: noted. I'll add a short DR appendix with commands and the manual verification checklist.

Maggie: don't forget to call out compliance benefits: chained ledger + signatures buys us attestations for audits.

Devon: lgtm overall. emphasise the audit trail and the default safety policies in the RFC.

Anya: will push updated RFC this afternoon. Ping me if you want to pair on the ledger schema.

Maggie: thanks — appreciate it. :raised_hands:
